title: AV Maintenance Checklist for Businesses, Churches and Institutions in Kenya
excerpt: A practical AV maintenance checklist for sound systems, conference rooms and LED screens in Kenya: what to check weekly, monthly and yearly, and when to call a technician.

focus_keywords: AV maintenance Kenya, sound system maintenance, AV support contract Kenya, LED screen maintenance
html:
Short answer: most AV failures come from dust, heat, unstable power, worn cables and changed settings. A simple routine of weekly user checks, monthly inspections and a yearly professional service keeps sound systems, boardrooms and LED screens reliable.

Weekly (by your own team)

  • Test every microphone and replace or charge batteries.
  • Check the display, camera and microphones in each meeting room before key meetings.
  • Confirm the mixer or control system is on its saved default scene.

Monthly

  • Inspect cables and connectors for damage, and secure loose cables.
  • Clean dust from amplifier racks, projectors and LED screen vents.
  • Check UPS and surge protection status.
  • Update conferencing software and room devices when updates are approved.

Yearly (professional service)

  • Full system test and re-tuning of speakers and equalisation.
  • Firmware updates and configuration backup for mixers, processors and control systems.
  • LED screen module, power supply and calibration check.
  • Report on worn equipment and a replacement plan.

When to call a technician

Call for help if you hear hum, crackling or feedback that was not there before, if a zone or speaker goes silent, if an LED screen shows dead modules or colour patches, or if meeting rooms fail to connect.

faqs.q: How often should a professional AV system be serviced?
faqs.a: At least once a year by a technician, with simple weekly and monthly checks by your own team. Heavily used systems such as churches and event venues may benefit from servicing every six months.

faqs.q: Do you maintain systems installed by other companies?
faqs.a: Yes. We can inspect, document and maintain existing systems, and recommend repairs or upgrades where needed.

faqs.q: What causes most AV system failures?
faqs.a: Dust, heat, unstable power and worn cables cause many failures, along with settings being changed by mistake. Surge protection, ventilation and saved default settings prevent most of them.
